```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
has_highs <- requireNamespace("highs", quietly = TRUE)
```

`postrank` constructs one common grade action from posterior directional-error
probabilities. Larger targets and smaller grades mean higher priority. Equal
grades withhold a comparison; they do not establish latent equality.

Model-independent core calculations always execute in this guide. Solver
chunks run only when the optional HiGHS package is installed; otherwise they are
shown without output. No Stan installation or scientific dataset is needed.
Gurobi examples are never executed here.

## A complete installed input

The newly authored example has 32 independent states from a specified proper
toy Normal law, three opaque IDs and two criteria. It is not an observed-data
fit, Alabama result or copied book oracle. The generator fixes S, seed and the
illustrative alpha allocation before generation.

```{r load-example}
library(postrank)
path <- system.file("examples", "synthetic-iid.json",
                    package = "postrank", mustWork = TRUE)
draws <- read_postrank_draws(path)
draws$entity_ids
draws$criterion_ids
dim(draws$joint_draws$tensor$values)
draws$validation[c("valid", "schema_checked", "source_values_checked",
                   "jointness_verified", "convergence_verified")]
```

The receipt separates semantic checks from scientific facts. R validation does
not run a general Draft 2020-12 validator or verify scientific jointness and
convergence. Input schema `applied-0.1`, derived API schema `0.1.0` and package
version are separate identifiers.

```{r inspect-generator}
generator <- system.file("examples", "make-synthetic-input.R",
                         package = "postrank", mustWork = TRUE)
source(generator)
payload <- make_postrank_synthetic_input()
rebuilt <- as_postrank_draws(payload)
stopifnot(identical(rebuilt$joint_draws$tensor$values,
                    draws$joint_draws$tensor$values))
names(payload)
payload$targets[[1]]
```

Sourcing defines the function without drawing values or writing files; the
function also preserves the caller RNG state. For your own data, replace the
targets, orientation, context, source origin, joint-state declaration and
original sampling history with facts. A bare array is insufficient. IDs are
character labels. Missing/nonfinite targets, unresolved identification,
observed entity ties and contradictory histories are rejected, without jitter
or hidden reordering.

Supported regimes are equal-weight joint states, criterionwise site-joint
states with their own sample counts, and explicit finite posterior laws with
safe-integer values and rational masses. Criterionwise expected loss does not
imply a joint cross-criterion trace. Finite-law arithmetic uses optional `gmp`;
it is not empirical draws renamed as an exact posterior. The optional
`posterior` adapter requires explicit variable and source-coordinate maps.

## Directional errors and a fixed action

`e[i,j,k]` estimates `P(theta[i,k] <= theta[j,k])`: the error when i is placed
above j. Diagonal NA sentinels are excluded; exact 0/1 values are not clipped.

```{r pairwise}
pairwise <- postrank_pairwise(draws, method = "blocks", block_size = 2L)
pairwise$sample_sizes
pairwise$e[, , "need_A"]
weights <- c(need_A = .6, need_B = .4)
grade <- setNames(c(1L, 2L, 2L), draws$entity_ids)
evaluation <- postrank_evaluate(grade, pairwise, weights, tau = .25)
evaluation[c("E_over_M", "E_over_N", "disclosure_rate", "weighted_risk")]
```

This user-supplied action places `001` above the others and withholds their
mutual comparison. It is not optimized. With M available unordered pairs and
N disclosed directions, risk is `(sum(weights*E)+tau*(M-N))/M`. `E_over_M`
and `E_over_N` have different denominators. Criterion-named weights are explicit
loss preferences and are not automatically normalized.

```{r all-abstain}
all_tie <- setNames(rep(1L, length(draws$entity_ids)), draws$entity_ids)
abstained <- postrank_evaluate(all_tie, pairwise, weights, tau = .25)
stopifnot(abstained$N == 0, all(is.na(abstained$E_over_N)),
          abstained$weighted_risk == .25)
abstained[c("N", "E_over_N", "weighted_risk")]
```

All-abstain has risk tau. A zero error numerator does not imply an error-free
ranking. Canonical positive-integer labels preserve the public pair relations.

## Build one shared problem

Building a model executes no optimizer.

```{r problems}
problem <- postrank_problem(pairwise, weights, tau = .25, G_max = 3L)
protected <- postrank_problem(pairwise, weights, .25, 3L,
                              q = c(need_B = .2))
exact_two <- postrank_problem(pairwise, weights, .25, 3L, exact_G = 2L)
minimax <- postrank_problem(pairwise, weights, .25, 3L, objective = "minimax")
stopifnot(identical(problem$input_identity, pairwise$input_identity))
problem$objective_units
minimax$objective_units
```

The main space permits at most G_max occupied grades. Exact-G requires exactly
G nonempty grades. Protection uses `E_k <= q_k*N`, even for zero-weight
criteria. Minimax minimizes the maximum of **expected criterion risks**, not
the expected draw-level maximum. Weighted risk is auxiliary for minimax.

Gurobi is the research default; HiGHS is an explicit alternative consuming the
same sparse problem. No failure triggers fallback. Availability reads metadata,
not a runtime/license test.

```{r backend-metadata}
availability <- postrank_backend_available("highs")
availability[c("installed", "available_for_attempt")]
```

Choose the desired native call. The Gurobi call is shown only.

```{r solve-example, eval=FALSE, purl=FALSE}
fit_gurobi <- postrank_solve(problem, backend = "gurobi",
  control = list(time_limit = 10, threads = 1L, seed = 1304L,
                 absolute_risk_gap = 1e-6, relative_gap = 0))
```

With HiGHS installed, the staged strategy (the default) solves the problem in
three stages:

1. Order dynamic programming and local search find a validated incumbent.
2. A weak-order linear relaxation with lazily added triangle inequalities gives
   a lower bound.
3. A strengthened label MIP runs only if a gap remains and the problem is
   small (`control$engine$mip_max_n`, 200 entities by default).

`strategy = "label_mip"` passes the label model unchanged.

```{r solve-highs, eval=has_highs}
control <- list(time_limit = 10, threads = 1L, seed = 1304L)
fit <- postrank_solve(problem, backend = "highs", control = control)
fit$status$normalized
fit$grade
unlist(fit$objective[c("risk_upper_bound", "risk_lower_bound",
                       "risk_absolute_gap")])
fit$objective$bound_source
unlist(fit$engine$stages$lp[c("status", "rounds", "cuts")])
```

The released grade is the independently validated incumbent. The upper bound is
its risk and the lower bound comes from the relaxation (or the MIP stage), so a
zero gap means the solver found no better grade for these coefficients, within
its tolerances; it is not a numerical certificate. A bound source ending in
`_clamped` means the reported bound exceeded the action's risk by no more than
the objective tolerance and was set equal to it; the fit warns, and warns again
if that excess is larger than the gap controls. A problem found infeasible
reports no lower bound. The gap says nothing about
Monte Carlo error in the coefficients or about the model.

Check raw/normalized status, incumbent existence, independent primal validation,
residuals and actual risk U/L/gap. Missing bounds remain NA. Weighted raw Z uses
`risk=tau+Z/M`; minimax t is already in risk units. Relative MIP gap is not
posterior regret. One incumbent does not enumerate every optimum.

The development machine required an explicitly selected project-local Gurobi
linkage repair for R 4.6, preserving the original host install. This is not a
general ABI guarantee. In that checkout the opt-in helper is
`checks/activate-project-runtime.R`, sourced in a fresh R session before loading
Gurobi. The package never activates libraries or relinks binaries; other systems
need their own compatible runtime and applicable license.

## Minimax as a secondary mode

Minimax refinement preserves the declared order of objectives: first the selected
criteria's maximum risk, then the **original** weighted risk. Original zero or
tiny positive weights are not replaced by a uniform perturbation. If there are
zero weights, a third stage minimizes uniformly weighted criterion risk while
preserving both preceding objectives; this resolves Pareto ties.

The internal weighted objective and cap are positively rescaled so small weights
are not lost to native absolute objective tolerances. Public risk units stay the
same. `fit$minimax_refine$lexicographic_certified` certifies the actual released
action for the primary and original weighted objectives.
`fit$minimax_refine$pareto_certified` additionally requires the third stage when
needed. Both are numerical statements under the recorded gaps and tolerances,
not formal certificates. If a stage is unavailable or uncertified, the result
records the reason and retains a validated action without claiming that stage.

Stage 1 receives a limit of three quarters of `time_limit`. The later stages and
fallbacks share the remaining budget; `fit$minimax_refine$time_limits` and the
stage optimization records expose the actual limits and scaling.
A selected criterion whose directional error probabilities are all at least tau
is degenerate: no action brings its risk below tau, so the minimax value is at
least tau, and equals tau (attained by all-tie) when all-tie is allowed. The
problem records such criteria and the fit warns about them.

```{r minimax-highs, eval=has_highs}
mm <- postrank_solve(minimax, backend = "highs", control = control)
mm$minimax_refine[c("mode", "applied", "improved", "reason")]
minimax$minimax_diagnostics$degenerate_criteria
```

## Side outputs: commonality cost and the tau frontier

The cost of a common grade compares each criterion's risk under the common grade
with that criterion's own minimum under the same tau and grade count. The
frontier tabulates disclosure and criterion error ratios over a tau grid. With
exact optima the number of disclosed pairs never falls as tau rises.

```{r side-outputs, eval=has_highs}
postrank_commonality_cost(fit, backend = "highs", control = control)$table[
  , c("criterion_id", "common_grade_risk", "own_best_risk", "cost_lower")]
frontier <- postrank_frontier(pairwise, weights, tau = c(.1, .25, .4),
                              G_max = 3L, backend = "highs", control = control)
frontier$table[, c("tau", "status", "N", "disclosure_rate",
                   "E_over_N_need_A", "E_over_N_need_B")]
```

## Practical Monte Carlo diagnostics

Two diagnostics show how much the Monte Carlo draws themselves move the decision.
Both are descriptive and give no finite-sample guarantee.

- Cross-fitting picks a grade on one half of the draws and evaluates it on the
  other half. For MCMC the halves are groups of whole chains.
- The fragility table flags pairs whose disclose-or-tie margin is within two
  Monte Carlo standard errors.

```{r mc-diagnostics, eval=has_highs}
cf <- postrank_crossfit(draws, fit = fit, backend = "highs", control = control)
cf
postrank_mc_fragility(draws, fit = fit)$summary
```

Posterior draws held in an `S x n x K` array can enter through
`postrank_draws_from_array()`. Its scientific declarations remain required
arguments, and for MCMC so is the chain layout (`chains`, `warmup_per_chain`,
`thin`); slot IDs, the draw index, the variable map and the chain history are
generated from them.

## Diagnostics and reporting

```{r diagnostics}
diagnostics <- postrank_diagnose(draws, grade = grade,
  settings = list(weights = weights, tau = .25, G_max = 3L))
diagnostics$summaries$weighted_total_loss$diagnostics$mcse_mean
stopifnot(!diagnostics$convergence_verified,
          !diagnostics$finite_sample_certificate)
```

These are descriptive IID standard errors for the toy fixture, not certificates.
For MCMC, optional `posterior` supplies Rhat, mean/bulk/tail ESS and MCSE.
Original chains/transitions, unequal counts, constant flags, raw NA/NaN,
warnings and errors are preserved. Unsupported metrics have explicit reasons;
unequal chains are not truncated. An all-abstain constant loss does not diagnose
target exploration. Joint loss is formed state by state to retain covariance;
criterionwise input does not fabricate total-loss MCSE. ESS is not an IID S.
After selecting a grade on the same draws, MCSE is post-selection descriptive.

```{r report-example, eval=FALSE, purl=FALSE}
if (isTRUE(fit$incumbent_validated)) {
  d <- postrank_diagnose(draws, fit = fit)
  postrank_report(fit, diagnostics = d,
                  output_file = "a-new-grade-report.html", lang = "en")
}
```

Reports separate posterior uncertainty, MC error, solver gap and policy
settings. Existing output files are not silently overwritten.

## Fixed-S IID reference calculations

This section is an appendix tool: a conditional reference for designs whose
sample sizes and alpha were fixed before sampling. The practical Monte Carlo
diagnostics above are the routine checks. The shipped generator fixed S=32, alpha=.05 and .025/.025 allocations before
generation. For real data these declarations must describe the actual design;
checking boxes after adaptive sampling does not establish that design.

```{r iid-reference}
design <- list(sample_sizes_fixed_before_sampling = TRUE,
               alpha_fixed_before_sampling = TRUE, adaptive_stopping = FALSE,
               planned_sample_sizes = c(need_A = 32L, need_B = 32L),
               declaration_note = "Fixed in the shipped toy generator before generation.")
bounds <- postrank_iid_bounds(draws, alpha = .05,
  alpha_by_criterion = c(need_A = .025, need_B = .025), design = design)
bounds[c("epsilon", "guarantee_status", "bound_computed", "numerically_verified",
          "finite_sample_certificate", "guarantee_issued")]
stopifnot(!bounds$numerically_verified, !bounds$finite_sample_certificate)
postrank_guarantee_capabilities()
```

Radii use M unordered pairs and actual criterion counts. They are
`theoretical_floating_reference`, with no verified outward enclosure or general
solver-bound certifier. `bound_computed=TRUE` issues no guarantee. Fixed-space
weighted regret uses `2*delta_w+eta` only with matching input, a validated
incumbent and the actual whole-problem absolute risk gap. Missing/rejected gaps
give `not_established`; q and minimax are outside that formula. q inner/outer
analysis is separately diagnostic, keeps thresholds outside [0,1] unclipped,
and never replaces the whole outer lower bound with an inner lower bound.
General MCMC, optional-stopping and minimax regret certificates are disabled.

## Serialization and repository producers

```{r roundtrip}
copy_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".json")
write_postrank_draws(draws, copy_path)
roundtrip <- read_postrank_draws(copy_path)
stopifnot(identical(roundtrip$joint_draws$tensor$values,
                    draws$joint_draws$tensor$values))
unlink(copy_path)
```

The strict JSON reader rejects decoded duplicate keys, malformed numbers,
unsafe integer metadata and invalid Unicode surrogates. Coordinates and
singleton axes are preserved. Reading does not assert general schema QA.

The installed core has 24 public functions. Repository `producers/R` modules
are separately sourced and are excluded from the installed package. The
reviewed Normal HB supports K=2, full observation, known SPD measurement V
and distinct sampled heterogeneity Sigma. It preserves independent
mu~N2(0,4I), Sigma~IW2(5,2I) priors. The checkout workflow below is displayed
only; supply actual labeled inputs and scientific metadata from its contract.

```{r stan-repository-workflow, eval=FALSE, purl=FALSE}
for (file in sort(list.files("producers/R", pattern = "[.]R$", full.names = TRUE)))
  source(file)
bundle <- postrank_normal_hb_data(y, V, entity_ids, criterion_ids, measurement)
config <- jsonlite::fromJSON("config/stan-runtime.json")
run <- run_postrank_stan("producers/stan/normal_hb.stan", bundle,
                         "results/a-new-unique-attempt", config, "my-reviewed-HB-run")
sampler_diagnostics <- diagnose_postrank_stan(run)
stan_draws <- export_postrank_stan_draws(run, scientific_metadata)
```

A known successful receipt binds reviewed source, actual JSON data, executable,
CSV hashes and original chain/transition histories. Target and shared HB states
are compared with raw CSV decoding. Structural export does not prove sampler
adequacy or model validity. Unknown imports, VB, Pathfinder and optimization
are not accepted as known MCMC. NUTS remains MCMC and warnings remain visible.

The repository's four single-cell engineering runs and bounded benchmark test
connectivity and failures, not statistical superiority or pilot precision.
Actual Alabama fitting/grading was not performed. Consult the README, phase
logs and reports for actual evidence and original-failure/recovery denominators.

## Citation and attribution

Use `citation("postrank")` for the versioned local software record and for
Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), whose posterior comparisons and integer grades
the method builds on. The weighted multicriteria risk equals their risk under
the mixture belief that picks a criterion with probability equal to its weight.
This is an applied validity check, not a new theorem. The postrank record
itself has no DOI and implies no CRAN publication. New code is MIT licensed. Preserved book oracles
have separate local-reuse provenance; external redistribution rights were not
established. Dependency licenses do not establish a license for those scripts.
The installed toy example contains no copied oracle values.
